 Tornadoes touch down in Del. and NJ as temperatures plummet 
 Tornadoes touched down in New Castle County, Del., and Burlington County, NJ, while hail fell in the Pennsylvania suburbs on Thursday, Nov. 12. 
 By Bill Henley , Brittney Shipp , David Chang , Robert Johnson and Emily Rose Grassi • 
 Published November 12, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 13, 2026 at 6:56 am 
 BOOKMARKER 
 What to Know
 A First Alert was in effect for the entire Philadelphia region on Thursday, Nov. 12, until 7 p.m. as severe storms brought a tornado to Delaware and New Jersey as well as hail to the Pennsylvania suburbs. 
 There were scattered storms across the region early Thursday morning. By the late morning into the afternoon, severe thunderstorms formed across the region. 
 A Tornado Watch was in effect for the entire region until 7 p.m. The National Weather Service confirmed that a tornado touched down in New Castle County, Delaware , early Thursday afternoon. 
 A Tornado Warning was also issued for Burlington and Mercer counties in New Jersey later in the afternoon. NBC10 confirmed a tornado touched down in Burlington County as well. 
 The severe storms also brought a massive amount of hail to the Philadelphia region .
 While the storms diminish into the evening, rain is still likely Thursday night and the wet weather will continue into Friday evening.
 Thursday night, a wind shift will dump colder air into the region. Temperatures will drop into the 40s with winds gusting up to 35 mph. Temperatures will feel like the 30s throughout Friday.
 Get the latest weather updates by downloading the NBC10 app and following the NBC10 First Alert Weather team .
 A First Alert was in effect for the Philadelphia region until 7 p.m. on Thursday due to severe storms that brought tornadoes to parts of Delaware and New Jersey as well as hail to the Pennsylvania suburbs. Get live updates below.

 Rain lingers into Friday morning before some see snow
 Day of destructive weather brings tornadoes, hail and heavy rain
 Several roads closed as crews assess damage in Burlington County
 Cold rain and some snow showers for Friday
 The same area of low pressure that brought severe storms including two tornadoes to our region Thursday (New Castle County, Delaware, and Burlington County, New Jersey) will bring a cold rain, snow showers and blustery winds as it departs.
 Expect a few showers this evening west of the city before a cold rain overtakes the region through the overnight hours. 
 A cold rain lingers in our neighborhoods Friday with some snow showers or flurries Friday evening into Friday night for the Pennsylvania suburbs. 
 Future Radar Legend 
 Green/Yellow = Rain
 Blue = Snow
 Pink = Rain mixes with snow
 This could lead to a light coating in the highest elevations, making for some tricky travel Friday evening into Saturday morning. 
 Temperatures will be in the 40s but it'll feel like the 30s all day Friday due to cold northwest winds that'll gust up to 30 mph. 
 Saturday will be mostly cloudy though dry with a cold start. 
 Wind chills will be in the upper 20s or low 30s Saturday morning before the breeze gradually diminishes Saturday evening. 
 Brighter and calmer winds take over for Sunday.
 National Weather Service plans surveys after 2 tornadoes
 Here are where our survey teams are headed for tomorrow to examine damage from the storms earlier this afternoon. The full results of those surveys will be issued sometime Friday afternoon or Friday evening. #NJwx #DEwx https://t.co/7bWuetoXsU
